newsitem.title: USA: Crime victims bill goes to Clinton.
newsitem.headline: Crime victims bill goes to Clinton.

text.p: The Senate Wednesday approved a bill that would ensure that victims of the Oklahoma City bombing can attend the trial of accused bomber Timothy McVeigh even though they would testify in the punishment phase of the trial if McVeigh is found guilty.

The bill would prevent judges from excluding victims from viewing a trial solely because they want to make an impact statement at the trial's conclusion. The measure, which cleared the House Wednesday, now goes to President Clinton.
The judge in the Oklahoma case has ruled that family members of victims may not watch court proceedings if they wish to testify in the sentencing phase of the trial.
The trial is set to start March 31 in Denver, Colorado.

The author of the measure, Representative Bill McCollum, a Florida Republican, said Wednesday it "achieves a balance between ensuring that fact witnesses are not influenced by other testimony at trial while providing every opportunity for victims and their families to see firsthand that our system is providing justice for them."
